findings.title: This maintenance removes every node in zone us-east-2a

calculation.formula: flagged when selectedInZone == totalInZone and other zones exist

findings.explanation: All 1 node(s) in zone us-east-2a are selected, so the zone leaves service entirely for the duration. Any workload whose replicas all sit in this zone loses every copy at once, and topology-spread constraints that require a pod per zone become unsatisfiable.

remediation.description: Take the zone's nodes in more than one wave

limitations: Whether losing a zone matters depends on the workloads in it. This check reports the topology fact, not its consequence.
Zone is read from the standard topology label. A node without that label is invisible to this check.

findings.title: Aggregate CPU is sufficient after removing the selected nodes

calculation.formula: free = allocatable - alreadyRequested; shortfall = needed - free

findings.explanation: The evicted pods request 150m of CPU and 3325m is free across the remaining nodes. This clears the aggregate check only — it is a necessary condition, not a guarantee that the scheduler can place every pod.
limitations: This is an aggregate sum, not a scheduling decision. Sufficient total capacity does not prove any individual pod fits on any individual node: ten nodes with 1 core free each cannot place a pod requesting 4 cores. Only the scheduler can answer that.

Scheduler predicates are not evaluated. Node selectors, affinity, taints, topology spread, and volume topology can each prevent placement regardless of free capacity. Those are covered by separate analyzers, which have their own limitations.
Uses resource *requests*, which is what the scheduler uses. A pod with no request counts as zero here and can still consume a node's actual CPU and memory at runtime.
Cordoned and not-Ready nodes are excluded from remaining capacity, since they accept no new pods.
Cluster autoscaling is not modelled. A cluster that would add nodes on demand may absorb this fine.

findings.title: Aggregate memory is sufficient after removing the selected nodes

calculation.formula: free = allocatable - alreadyRequested; shortfall = needed - free

findings.explanation: The evicted pods request 102Mi of memory and 6Gi is free across the remaining nodes. Aggregate check only.
limitations: This is an aggregate sum, not a scheduling decision. Sufficient total capacity does not prove any individual pod fits on any individual node: ten nodes with 1 core free each cannot place a pod requesting 4 cores. Only the scheduler can answer that.

Scheduler predicates are not evaluated. Node selectors, affinity, taints, topology spread, and volume topology can each prevent placement regardless of free capacity. Those are covered by separate analyzers, which have their own limitations.
Uses resource *requests*, which is what the scheduler uses. A pod with no request counts as zero here and can still consume a node's actual CPU and memory at runtime.
Memory cannot be oversubscribed the way CPU can. A pod exceeding its limit is killed, not throttled, so headroom here is less forgiving than it looks.

findings.title: PodDisruptionBudget demo/web-pdb permits this disruption
findings.explanation: 1 covered pod(s) sit on the selected nodes and the budget allows 1 voluntary disruption(s). This is the constraint that limits how many nodes may be taken at once.
limitations: A snapshot-time reading. Headroom shrinks if other maintenance or a rollout consumes it before this operation runs.
